finalText:
**Redis crashed, took down the whole system.**

Here's the chain: Redis connection failed at 02:14:07. The cache layer immediately fell back to direct database reads, causing massive cache miss storms on the orders table. The database got overloaded, requests started timing out, and since timeouts still occupy queue slots, the backlog piled up — starting at 52 requests, climbing to 568 by 02:31. Each request took 5+ seconds to timeout, so new requests arrived faster than old ones cleared. Eventually the request backlog consumed all heap memory. Worker-2 crashed with out-of-memory at 02:31:44. The api became unresponsive 8 seconds later and the supervisor killed the whole process group.

The system had no circuit breaker — it just kept queueing failed requests instead of failing fast. Redis tried to reconnect 12 times and failed each time (ECONNREFUSED on 10.0.0.12:6379).

**To recover**: Restart Redis, then the app should come back online. To prevent it next time, add circuit breaker logic to reject requests once the queue hits a threshold, and make sure Redis has failover or monitoring so it doesn't silently die.
